prompt: In the plain SHA-256 store, what did `vcrypt audit` reveal without reversing anything?

choices.text: Ana's password
choices.why: Nothing was reversed.

choices.text: Which accounts share a password
choices.why: Right: equal passwords, equal values.

choices.text: The length of every password in the store
choices.why: Digests are 64 digits whatever the password.

choices.text: The key used to hash them
choices.why: SHA-256 has no key.

prompt: `printf 'Vereda@2026' | sha256sum` printed exactly Ana's stored value. Why does that matter for a store that leaks?
hint: Who else gets this same value?

choices.text: It shows the store was not encrypted at rest
choices.why: Encryption at rest is a different question.

choices.text: Precomputed lists work against it
choices.why: Right: the digest is the same in every system.

choices.text: It proves SHA-256 has been broken
choices.why: SHA-256 worked exactly as designed.

choices.text: It reveals the server's pepper
choices.why: There is no pepper in this store.

prompt: How many different stored values does the plain SHA-256 store of the eight accounts contain?
hint: The first line of the audit.

choices.text: Yes, it must be kept apart from the hashes
choices.why: That describes a pepper.

choices.text: No, it is stored beside the hash
choices.why: Right: it is needed to verify.

choices.text: Only in bcrypt
choices.why: No scheme keeps the salt secret.

choices.text: Yes, it is the encryption key of the password
choices.why: Nothing is encrypted; it is mixed in before hashing.

prompt: Salted SHA-256 removed the shared values. Which problem of the plain store does it leave untouched?

choices.text: Precomputed lists
choices.why: A list would need computing per salt; that is solved.

choices.text: Equal passwords being visible
choices.why: The audit found none.

choices.text: The billions of guesses a second
choices.why: Right: a salted fast hash is still fast.

choices.text: The length of the stored line
choices.why: Length was never a problem.

prompt: A system gives each user one salt at registration and keeps it for every later password. What does an observer of successive stores learn?
hint: Same salt, same password, same value.

choices.text: Each user's password, from two stores
choices.why: Two values do not reveal a password.

choices.text: When a user goes back to an earlier password
choices.why: Right: a salt is new on every change.

choices.text: Which users share a password
choices.why: Different users still have different salts.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: Reuse is visible.

prompt: Match each stored prefix to its algorithm.
hint: From the three lines of the capture.

prompt: What makes Argon2id harder for GPUs and custom chips than PBKDF2?

choices.text: It needs memory per guess
choices.why: Right: memory is what they cannot cheaply multiply.

choices.text: It uses a longer salt
choices.why: Both use 16-byte salts here.

choices.text: It is a secret algorithm
choices.why: It is RFC 9106.

choices.text: It uses SHA-512 instead of SHA-256
choices.why: Argon2 uses BLAKE2 internally; that is not why.

prompt: Beyond how many bytes of a password does bcrypt ignore the rest?
Why are the cost parameters written into each stored string rather than only in the application's configuration?
hint: What happens the day the cost is raised?

choices.text: So an attacker knows how hard each guess will be
choices.why: That is a side effect, not the reason.

choices.text: Because the standards forbid configuration files
choices.why: No standard says that.

choices.text: To make the stored line longer and harder to read
choices.why: Length adds nothing.

choices.text: Old hashes still say how to verify them
choices.why: Right: raising the cost does not break them.

prompt: Where should Vereda keep its pepper?

choices.text: In a column of the users table
choices.why: Then a leak of the table includes it.

choices.text: In a secrets manager or an HSM
choices.why: Right: apart from the database.

choices.text: In the application's repository
choices.why: Lesson 17 says why not.

choices.text: Beside each hash, like a salt
choices.why: That would make it a salt.

prompt: An attacker obtains `store-peppered.txt` through a database injection, but not the pepper. What can they do with the right password for Ana?
hint: The third command of the pepper capture.

choices.text: Confirm it, slowly
choices.why: Without the pepper it does not even verify.

choices.text: Recover the pepper from Ana's line
choices.why: The pepper is not in the line.

choices.text: Nothing: even a correct guess fails
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Sign in as Ana directly
choices.why: The store holds no session.

prompt: A pepper is one secret for the whole system, while a ___ is different for every account and not secret.
Verification said `rehash now: stored m=7168,t=1 is below the policy`. When can the application compute the new hash?

choices.text: In a nightly batch job over the whole store
choices.why: Nobody knows the passwords to recompute them.

choices.text: Right now, during this sign-in
choices.why: Right: the only moment it holds the password.

choices.text: Only after the user resets the password
choices.why: No reset is needed.

choices.text: Never: old hashes stay as they are
choices.why: Leaving them is how weak hashes accumulate.

prompt: Why did `vcrypt verify` answer a missing account, `ana.lim`, with the same words as a wrong password?
hint: What would a different answer tell a stranger?

choices.text: Because the tool does not check whether accounts exist
choices.why: It does: it looked the user up first.

choices.text: To save one Argon2id computation
choices.why: Saving it would make the paths differ in time.

choices.text: To keep membership private
choices.why: Right: on a clinic's portal that is a health fact.

choices.text: Because ana.lim is close to ana.lima
choices.why: The answer is the same for any missing name.

prompt: Vereda moves from bcrypt to Argon2id. Which steps belong to the migration? Choose all that apply.
hint: Both accepted on the way in.

choices.text: Accept bcrypt and Argon2id hashes when verifying
choices.why: Yes: old accounts still sign in.

choices.text: Write Argon2id whenever a bcrypt hash verifies
choices.why: Yes: the upgrade on sign-in.

choices.text: After a deadline, require a reset for accounts still on bcrypt
choices.why: Yes: no weak hash stays forever.

choices.text: Convert every bcrypt hash to Argon2id in one batch
choices.why: Impossible without the passwords.
